author: cmungall
body:
* **InterPro ID / label**
  IPR020536 "ThiI, AANH domain", mapped to GO:0004810 CCA tRNA nucleotidyltransferase activity.

* **Example sequences with problematic annotation (ID + gene/protein name):**
  * P77718 thiI, tRNA sulfurtransferase (*Escherichia coli* K-12)
  * O34595 thiI, probable tRNA sulfurtransferase (*Bacillus subtilis* 168)
  * A0KZA4 thiI (*Shewanella* sp. ANA-3)

* **Description of issue**
  ThiI is the tRNA 4-thiouridine (s4U8) synthase. Its AANH (adenine nucleotide alpha hydrolase-like) domain activates U8 with ATP before sulfur transfer from IscS [PMID:15037613]. It has no CCA-adding activity. The correct MF is GO:0140741 tRNA-uracil-4 sulfurtransferase activity (EC 2.8.1.4, RHEA:24176).

  All 287 Swiss-Prot entries that carry RHEA:24176 receive GO:0004810 from IEA:InterPro, alongside the correct GO:0140741 from EC2GO. On *E. coli* ThiI, the wrong term sits next to EcoCyc's IDA for sulfurtransferase activity.

  Suggested fix: remap IPR020536 to GO:0140741, or drop the MF mapping if the domain is considered too broad.

  Found while checking Swiss-Prot RHEA annotations against native GO annotations ([analysis](https://github.com/ai4curation/ai-gene-review/blob/claude/zen-meitner-rsk71c/projects/RHEA/RHEA-SWISSPROT-COMPLETENESS.md)).
title: InterPro2GO issue: IPR020536 ThiI, AANH domain > GO:0004810 CCA tRNA nucleotidyltransferase activity
